paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. Jesus doesn't open with a pep talk. He says, "The time is fulfilled," and "the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!" (Mark 1:15). That's the oven timer going off: the moment has come, and He's inviting you in.

Now look at who He calls. Simon, Andrew, James and John are in the middle of regular work, casting a net and mending a net (Mark 1:16, 19). Jesus says, "Come, follow Me," and promises, "I will make you fishers of men" (Mark 1:17). I think the point is that He does the making. They don't have to show up already finished, and honestly, I got called out of a junk drawer, so I'm the last one to say you need a perfect résumé.

The other thing I see is how real the cost is. They "left their nets and followed Him," and James and John left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men (Mark 1:18, 20). Following Jesus isn't a hobby you squeeze in between other things, friend. So when He calls you through His Word, you don't have to have it all figured out. Just answer, and let Him do the making.
